front: What is the legal class of a standard Type 56 SKS (23 Oct 2026)?
back: Non restricted (99%, RCMP Firearms Reference Table, valid 19 Oct 2026). Under federal review: check each season.

front: How many rounds may your SKS magazine hold?
back: 5. A semi automatic centrefire long gun magazine over 5 is a prohibited device (99%, SOR/98-462 Part 4).

front: Type 56 SKS vs Type 56 AK?
back: Same Chinese name, different guns. The Type 56 AK (AK-47 copy) is prohibited; the Type 56 SKS is non restricted (99%, FRT).

front: Why shake the SKS bolt before firing?
back: The firing pin floats free. It must rattle. Stuck forward in old grease, it can slam fire (70%).

front: What is a slam fire?
back: The rifle fires as the bolt closes, with no trigger press, usually from a stuck firing pin (70%).

front: Who checks headspace on a surplus rifle?
back: A qualified gunsmith, with gauges (Tip). Too much headspace can split or rupture cases (80%).

front: SKS safety: which way is SAFE?
back: Forward and up. It blocks the trigger. Rearward and down is fire (95%, TC 9-56).

front: Does the SKS safety stop a slam fire?
back: No. It blocks the trigger only (95%, my reading of TC 9-56).

front: How do you empty the SKS fixed magazine?
back: Safety on, pull the magazine catch back: it swings open and the rounds drop out (95%).

front: Magazine emptied. Is the SKS unloaded?
back: Not yet. Close it, pull the handle back to eject the chambered round, then look in chamber, bore and magazine (95%).

front: Where does the stripper clip go?
back: Into the clip guides at the front of the open bolt carrier. Thumb presses the rounds down (95%).

front: SKS in the truck: what must be empty?
back: The chamber AND the fixed magazine, because it is always attached (99%, synopsis page 11 item 28).

front: Function check: safety on, trigger pressed. What should happen?
back: Nothing. The hammer must not fall. Safety off: it falls (95%, TC 9-56).

front: Rear sight leaf: what do the numbers mean?
back: Hundreds of metres: 1 is 100 m, 10 is 1000 m. First mark: battle setting up to 300 m (95%).

front: Group hits low. Front post up or down?
back: Down. Move the front sight opposite to the miss (85%).

front: Why does corrosive ammo rust a rifle?
back: Fired chlorate primers leave salt; the salt pulls water from the air (65%). Wash with water, dry, oil, same day.

front: Surplus FMJ (full metal jacket) for deer in BC?
back: Illegal. Hunt with expanding bullets only (99%, synopsis page 12).

front: SKS field strip: 7 parts in order?
back: Top cover, recoil spring, bolt carrier, bolt, gas tube, gas piston, trigger group if needed (95%, TC 9-56).

front: Recoil spring goes back in which end first?
back: Stepped end first, into the bolt carrier (95%, TC 9-56).

front: Bolt back in: where is the extractor?
back: Right front, rear of the bolt about 10 mm from the receiver wall (95%).

front: 7.62x39 123 gr: energy at 100 yd and 200 yd?
back: About 1,136 and 842 ft lb (75%, Hornady data). Under 1,000 ft lb past about 130 m.

front: Your SKS deer range limit?
back: 150 m at most, and only if you pass the plate test (Tip).

front: Barrel cut under 470 mm on an SKS?
back: Restricted. Cut from a rifle to under 457 mm: prohibited (99%, Criminal Code s. 84(1); FRT records).

front: Folding stock that fires under 660 mm?
back: Makes the rifle restricted (99%, s. 84(1)). A bullpup stock is a prohibited device (99%).

front: Suppressor for the SKS?
back: A prohibited device in Canada (99%, Criminal Code s. 84(1)).
